   "Revenue quality caveats: NRR of about 900% is called unrealistic for mature cohorts. Media-reported policy-violating customers were 5-7% of 9M26 revenue (about $1.7-2.3B by CG estimate), possibly including distillation. Revenue is 79% consumption-based, so growth could be volatile.",

Over 80% of Q3 revenue came from models released in the prior six months.",

  "insights": [
   "GS reiterates Buy on CSGP with a 12-month price target of $36 vs $30.20 price, 19.2% upside. The call rests on a gradual organic revenue recovery and margin expansion as the more visible earnings catalyst.",

   "US multifamily vacancy fell from a peak of 8.5% in 4Q 2025 to 7.9% in 3Q 2026. CoStar forecasts 7.6% by 4Q 2027 as deliveries fall from 447k to 303k. GS expects this to support Apartments.com budgets and reduce ad-tier downsell.",
   "Apartments.com organic growth slowed to 6% y/y in 3Q 2026 from 9% in 2Q and 10% in 1Q, well below its 17% 10-year average. Causes are customer cost-cutting, competitor pricing, small-property cancellations and weak sales capacity. CoStar guides to mid-single digits in 4Q 2026.",

  "insights": [
   "Higher inflation and interest rates are keeping stock-bond correlations positive, weakening a core assumption of the traditional 60/40 portfolio.",

   "Post-pandemic inflation forced a sharp rate reset that hit both bond prices and equity valuations. Bonds still provide income but may not diversify enough on their own.",
   "Fidelity outlines a 60/20/20 framework in which equities stay the anchor, bonds keep the income role, and part of the bond sleeve goes to assets with low or negative correlation to stocks and bonds.",
   "Bitcoin combines gold-like scarcity from limited supply with technology network growth viewed through Metcalfe's law. It may act as a store of value in some environments and a higher-growth risk asset in others.",
   "Bitcoin may sit alongside gold in the diversifying sleeve, so an allocation could be funded from the 40% bond allocation rather than the 60% equity allocation.",
   "Neither bitcoin nor gold generates cash flows, so DCF does not apply. One alternative is comparing price with its long-term power-law curve and historical support trend.",

 {
  "source": "Goldman Sachs",
  "title": "Global Markets Daily: AI and The Dollar: Making It or Breaking It",
  "type": "fx",
  "priority": "high",
  "published": "2026-11-26",
  "insights": [
   "GS G10 FX strategy argues the Dollar is linked to AI-related equity performance. An AI selloff with rest-of-world outperformance was expected to be a catalyst for Dollar depreciation.",
   "Recent price action shows the balance is fine. The AI correction took US relative equity performance off the highs, but DXY reached new highs.",
   "Recent DXY moves are well explained by US 2-year yields, risk sentiment, and relative equity returns (Exhibit 1). Safe-haven characteristics have been clearly on display in recent weeks.",
   "AI selloffs are most clearly USD negative when the broader risk backdrop stays supported, as on November 5 after the US midterm elections, which GS equity strategists called a rotation within equities.",
   "When an AI selloff spills into broader risk sentiment, the Dollar tends to appreciate even with relative US equity underperformance. Some October days were exceptions, reflecting rate relief in European assets.",
   "The share of days when the S&P 500 also falls during an AI selloff has risen, while the share when it rises has fallen. Cross-asset sentiment has become more sensitive to AI.",
   "Policymakers are focused on the risk. Almost all FOMC minutes participants flagged AI investment disappointment under financial stability, and AI was the top concern in the Financial Stability Report survey.",
   "Higher equity volatility makes the Dollar less sensitive to relative equity returns, so near-term Dollar weakness on AI selloffs is less likely.",
   "Over the medium term a more negative AI view is still Dollar-negative. Weaker forward capex expectations and fading AI price pressures would erode support the Dollar had in 2026.",
   "GS estimates AI contributed roughly one-third of cumulative DXY appreciation through October 2026, assuming AI drives most of the growth-expectations impulse and about half of the policy-rate impulse.",
   "GS baseline is a gradual peaking of AI investment and less AI-led US equity outperformance, weighing on the Dollar over time. The key risk is a rapid reassessment that creates at least temporary Dollar demand.",

   "Crowding remains somewhat elevated, with the median hedge fund holding 70% of its long portfolio in its top 10 positions. CTA beta to Tech/Momentum is modestly negative, leaving fast money less exposed to a continued reversal.",

  "insights": [
   "Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia CEO before the US open Monday and NVDA rose 31.5% in a large short squeeze after shorts were added into the end of last week. Privorotsky asks whether the Trump put is back.",
   "Huang's return reduces doubt about Nvidia's willingness to keep underwriting the AI buildout, and his alignment with the administration may make him lean in harder. CoreWeave rose 22%.",

   "China barely participated, with CSI 300 +0.14% and Hang Seng -0.73% in early trade. Tighter US rules on remote access to advanced chips are the backdrop, and Commerce licensing for offshore data center access is the first thing to watch.",

   "Chinese 10yr yield at 1.586% is at or near year, 5yr and decade lows, read as a structurally unencouraging signal on China growth and disinflation.",

 {
  "source": "Natixis",
  "title": "The NVIDIA affair brings Trump and Xi closer",
  "type": "macro",
  "priority": "medium",
  "published": "2026-11-26",
  "insights": [
   "Jensen Huang resigned as NVIDIA CEO on about 12 November amid a US national-security probe into chip diversion to China, then was reinstated on 23 November, eleven days later. The author says the affair has drawn Trump and Xi closer rather than breaking the d\u00e9tente.",
   "At the APEC summit in Shenzhen, Xi reaffirmed the 'constructive relationship of strategic stability' and the two sides agreed to draft an action plan. Bessent said H200 sales policy to China is unchanged, and Trump suggested Blackwell chips could be sold to China in two or three years.",
   "Trump owns the H200 decision, and a collapse of the d\u00e9tente would support critics who say chips were given away for nothing. Xi needs the 'back door' of licensed, smuggled or rented NVIDIA compute to train frontier models until China's own AI stack can stand alone.",
   "The back door is narrowing. A US Commerce rule effective on the summit day requires a licence for any data centre worldwide giving Chinese-headquartered firms large-scale access to advanced AI compute.",
   "The two administrations diverge from the leaders. Commerce is tightening controls, both parties back chip-export restrictions in the 2027 defence bill, and the Democrats take control of Congress from January. The AI Overwatch Act would let lawmakers block sales to adversaries.",
   "Commerce approved 879,868 NVIDIA H200 and equivalent AMD chips for Chinese firms between December 2025 and May 2026, including firms on the Pentagon's Chinese military companies list, according to records released by Rep. Brian Mast.",
   "NVIDIA's share of China's specialised AI hardware market fell from 95% to zero as Beijing steered firms to Huawei. NVIDIA chips are allowed only when strictly necessary, for training advanced models.",

 {
  "source": "Natixis",
  "title": "The NVIDIA affair brings Trump and Xi closer",
  "type": "macro",
  "priority": "medium",
  "published": "2026-11-26",
  "insights": [
   "Jensen Huang resigned as NVIDIA CEO on 12 November amid a US national-security probe into chip diversion to China, and was reinstated on 23 November, eleven days later. The expected destabilisation of the Trump-Xi d\u00e9tente did not happen.",
   "At the APEC summit in Shenzhen the two leaders reaffirmed a 'constructive relationship of strategic stability' and agreed to draft an action plan. Bessent said the H200 sales policy to China is unchanged.",
   "Trump suggested Blackwell chips could be sold to China in two or three years, and publicly backed Huang as a 'national treasure'. NVIDIA's board cited input from 'senior levels' of the US government in reinstating him.",
   "The affair makes the leaders co-dependent. Trump needs the relationship to deliver to defend the H200 decision before a hostile Congress, while Xi needs the back door to NVIDIA hardware until China's own AI stack can stand alone.",
   "The d\u00e9tente has delivered less than hoped. NVIDIA's share of China's specialised AI hardware market fell from 95% to zero as Beijing steered firms to Huawei, allowing NVIDIA chips only for training advanced models.",
   "Executive and legislative branches are diverging from the leaders. Commerce is tightening controls, a new rule requires a licence for any data centre worldwide giving Chinese-headquartered firms large-scale advanced AI compute access, and Congress is moving to codify curbs.",
   "Democrats will control Congress from January and both parties back chip-export restrictions in the 2027 defence bill. The AI Overwatch Act would let lawmakers block sales to adversaries.",
   "Rep. Brian Mast released records showing Commerce approved 879,868 NVIDIA H200 and equivalent AMD chips for Chinese firms between December 2025 and May 2026, including firms on the Pentagon's Chinese military companies list.",
   "NVIDIA's board set up a national security and export control committee of independent directors and is hiring a chief compliance officer. Huang is back but under watch.",
   "Key dates are the trade truce expiry on 10 January and the G20 meeting in December. Beijing's retaliation tools are rare-earth licensing, paused but not dismantled, and a faster shift to Huawei Ascend chips.",
   "Europe is a bystander exposed on two fronts. It depends on NVIDIA hardware, Chinese rare earths and mature chips, and the new data-centre rule could restrict its access to advanced US chips if Chinese firms trained models there."

   "The grid, not generation, is the bottleneck. US interconnection queues hold about 2,060 GW with median waits over 5 years, large transformers are short for up to four years, and a leading European grid-equipment maker reported a record backlog of about \u20ac51B with a 1.5x book-to-bill.",
